subject: POC trial planning - workload profile & next steps (Acme Analytics)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@acme-analytics.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: POC planning call — workload intake & next steps

Hi Laura & Tom,

Great to meet earlier — appreciate the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side to get the POC (trial) scoped and scheduled.

1) Success criteria (what Acme will measure):
   - Latency: 95th pctile < 300ms for interactive queries (under expected concurrency)
   - Throughput: sustain ~120 QPS average for inference path during peak window
   - Cost: targeted inference cost <= $0.004 / 1k tokens (post-quantization)
   - Quality: precision on entity extraction >= 92% on your eval set

2) Evaluation plan / timeline (proposed):
   - Week 0 (this week): exchange workload profile & sample data; agree on success criteria (owner: Acme / Laura)
   - Week 1: Redwood spins up POC environment and ingests sample workload; baseline performance tests (owner: Redwood - Ben/Dylan)
   - Week 2: End-to-end eval with your eval set; iterate on model/configs (owner: joint)
   - Week 3: Final report & recommendations; decision meeting

3) Ownership & contacts:
   - Acme: Laura Chen (POC owner), Tom Alvarez (eng lead)
   - Redwood: Ben Carter (sales lead), Marissa Cole (customer success), Dylan Brooks (solutions eng)

4) Immediate ask: please complete the attached workload intake (acme_workload_profile.csv) with the following items filled where possible:
   - RPS average and 95th percentile during business hours
   - Typical and max token lengths (input + expected response)
   - Concurrent sessions/batches expected
   - Burst patterns (e.g., hourly spikes, daily batch jobs)
   - Any hard SLO windows (e.g., 9am-5pm EST)

Attachment: acme_workload_profile.csv (CSV, 2 KB) — small template with sample rows.

Proposed next meeting: Tue Feb 23, 10:00 AM PT to review the filled intake and align on timeline. If that works for you, we’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

--
Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference for engineering teams

From: Laura Chen <laura@acme-analytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: POC planning call — workload intake & next steps

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the clear summary. We’re aligned on the success criteria broadly — a couple of clarifications:

- Latency SLO: that 300ms 95th looks good for interactive queries; offline batch scoring can be looser.
- Volume: our global peak currently ~150 QPS for the scoring endpoint, but the subset going through the new pipeline will be ~80–120 QPS during peak after rollout; average closer to 40 QPS.
- Token lengths: typical user query + model response averages ~350 tokens combined; max observed ~2,400 tokens for long-form reports (rare).
- Concurrency: up to 180 concurrent requests during spikes (we queue some requests on our side).
- Burst patterns: daily peak at 9am ET (30–45 min burst), and a large nightly batch job at 02:00 UTC that will peak for ~20 minutes.

I’ve filled the attached CSV with the numbers we discussed and attached a small eval set sample (eval_samples.jsonl) for your tests.

We can do Tue Feb 23 10:00 AM PT — please send invite.

Cheers,
Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Product, Acme Analytics
laura@acme-analytics.com | +1 212-555-0199

Attachments: acme_workload_profile.csv (CSV, 5 KB), eval_samples.jsonl (JSONL, 150 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@acme-analytics.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: POC planning call — workload intake & next steps

Laura / Tom — thanks for the quick turn. I reviewed the intake and the eval samples — very helpful.

Quick notes and proposed POC plan (updated):
- We’ll target an initial config using an LLM variant with int8 quantization for cost parity; Dylan will run a few performance permutations to find the best latency/cost point.
- Baseline run: Redwood will provision a dedicated staging pool (same region as your users) and run a 24-hour soak test using your supplied traffic profile (owner: Dylan).
- Spike testing: we’ll replay your daily 9am ET burst and the nightly batch to validate autoscaling and queue behavior.
- Data handling: we’ll use ephemeral logs for the POC; if you need retention longer than 7 days, let us know (security/compliance tie-in).

Proposed timeline:
- Tue Feb 23: alignment call (10:00 AM PT) — calendar invite will go out in a minute.
- Wed Feb 24: Redwood prepares staging environment and begins baseline tests (Dylan).
- Mon Mar 1: joint evaluation review, preliminary findings, and config recommendations.

Open question for Acme: do you want us to simulate the ~2,400 token long-form requests during the POC or treat those as outliers for a separate run? If you want them included, we’ll need to scale the staging instance size accordingly.

Next steps:
- Dylan, can you confirm instance sizing and whether we need GPU types that handle 2.4k token sequences efficiently?
- Laura / Tom, confirm if long-form request simulation should be included in the baseline.

Thanks — invite sent.

-Ben
Attachment: poc-success-criteria.docx (DOCX, 24 KB)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@acme-analytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 17:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: POC planning call — workload intake & next steps

Hi all — looping in with technical plan and a couple clarifying questions.

Plan:
- I’ll spin up a dedicated staging cluster (NVidia A10x or similar) and run both the interactive and batch profiles. For int8 quantized runs we typically start with 4x A10x for the kind of throughput you described, then scale based on observed 95th pctile latency.
- For 2.4k token sequences: those change GPU memory usage significantly. If you want those simulated as part of the baseline, we’ll provision a larger instance (A100-class) for the spike windows to avoid OOMs.
- Concurrency handling: we’ll test with both continuous RPS replay and bursty fan-out patterns to validate queue/timeout behavior.

Questions for Acme (quick):
1) Are the 2.4k token requests typically single-turn or multi-turn (i.e., do they include a long conversation history)?
2) Do you need us to retain model outputs for debugging beyond 7 days for this POC? If so, we’ll enable longer retention and coordinate with your security team.

I’ll post the initial sizing and estimated cost delta for including the long-form tests by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
